Research and data support

Research and data support turns market, prospect and spreadsheet data into checked reports.

Use market and competitor research to compare vendors, prices or products against the same criteria. We record the source and date for each finding, so you can see which details are verified and which need a follow-up before you act.

Our data entry and cleanup work can combine approved exports, standardise fields and flag duplicates or missing values. You get a spreadsheet with the source links and a short note on the records that still need review before anyone uses them.

When this support helps

Compare vendors before a decision

Use the same fields for each vendor and record where a published claim needs confirmation, such as availability or included features.

Prepare a list before outreach

Check that each account matches the target audience, keep the source and remove duplicates before the list is reviewed.

Clean a report that keeps drifting

Trace the fields back to the source, agree one definition for each metric and give the team a repeatable refresh checklist.

Planning your support

Turn market and competitor research into a comparison

In this fictional example, a founder needs to compare six providers before choosing which ones to interview.

Their websites describe different packages and some prices depend on volume or contract length. Research and data support produces a comparison the founder can check, with a source for each finding and a separate list of questions to ask.

  1. 01

    Agree the question and comparison fields

    Before starting market and competitor research, confirm the audience, region, inclusion rules and the decision the research will inform. Use the same fields for every provider, such as service scope, pricing basis, relevant restrictions and evidence date. Mark anything that can only be answered in a sales conversation.

  2. 02

    Collect and check the records

    Use the approved sources and record the relevant page, access date and detail for each field. Data entry and cleanup can normalise units and remove duplicates while keeping the original values available. If two sources disagree, note both and indicate which one is newer or closer to the provider.

  3. 03

    Deliver the brief with the evidence

    Use research and data support to prepare a sortable workbook and a short findings note. Identify where published figures can be compared and where the commercial basis differs. Keep unverified fields visible in the findings note so a blank cell is never mistaken for a confirmed result. Give the reviewer the source links and follow-up questions so they can verify the most important fields before making a decision.

Handle gaps in data entry and cleanup

Record the source, what you checked and who can decide. Keep blocked work visible until the next action changes.

Two sources describe different offers

Keep the original claims and dates separate. Market and competitor research can record that one page describes a trial and another describes a paid plan, or that a feature was described in a different region. Flag the comparison field for the reviewer instead of combining incompatible records.

A row has missing or disputed data

Keep the record with its missing fields marked. Data entry and cleanup can link likely duplicates for review and record why a match is uncertain. If the gap affects a decision, show the missing evidence and a way the reviewer could verify it.

A source is outside the agreed scope

Record that a field could not be verified from the available sources and ask the owner whether to use an alternative. If the work requires a new login, export or personal data, pause that part of the research and data support until the authorised scope is confirmed.

Define the brief for market and competitor research

Search criteria and sources

Share the questions for market and competitor research, the sources you consider acceptable, and any topics or records to exclude. Give a valid and an invalid example so the researcher can see where the inclusion rule matters. Agree when you want a second source for a claim.

Data entry and cleanup format

Define required columns, date and currency formats, and the fields that identify a duplicate. Decide how to label unknown, conflicting and unverified values. Share a sample row and what you want preserved from the original if a spreadsheet is transformed for import.

Output and review owner

Name who will check the first batch of research and data support. Agree the format, turnaround, permissions and how the findings will be used. For regular reporting, document the source query, definition, period and refresh date so the next batch can be reproduced.

Check the quality of research and data support

Check the trail back to the source

Sample a few rows and open the evidence behind the most important fields. Check publication or access date, spelling, units and whether the selected detail really supports the claim. Useful market and competitor research should make it possible to repeat this check without starting over.

Check structured output before use

For data entry and cleanup, compare an original record and a transformed row side by side. Confirm that required fields are present and that a changed value, removed duplicate or unresolved mismatch is documented. Review import field mapping on a small batch first.

Check the summary against the question

Ask whether research and data support answered the decision you originally posed. Review the gaps as well as the findings. Confirm which differences are supported by evidence, which may reflect varying scope, and what follow-up would resolve remaining uncertainty.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you research competitors or markets?

Yes. Agree the markets, questions and comparable fields first. We return sources, dates and any important differences in how the information was reported.

Can you build a prospect list?

We can prepare a list using your targeting and source rules, verify entries and mark missing information for review. Your team decides who may be contacted.

What happens if a source is unclear?

We mark the field as uncertain or missing and explain the conflicting evidence. You can review the record before it is used.

Can you clean or annotate an existing dataset?

Share an authorised sample and the intended format or labelling rubric. We review the first batch against the rules before continuing.

Can you prepare recurring reports?

Yes. Agree the source, refresh schedule, metric definitions and the decisions the report should support.

What formats can the work be delivered in?

Agree the output before setup. A checked spreadsheet, CSV import, research memo, chart or dashboard update can all be scoped around the same source record.
